plain.li: [greetings,warm,their:linesmen] Your letter came down the line clear as morning, {WRITER}, and every mast between us passed it on gladly.
[greetings,cordial,their:linesmen] The relay has your letter, {WRITER}. Heard at the ridge mast, written down at ours.
[greetings,cool,their:linesmen] We have your letter. The line carries every voice, and yours is one of them, nothing more yet.
[news,warm,their:linesmen] The masts hear the whole region, {WRITER}, and we always say where. Here is what the season sent down the line.
[news,cordial,their:linesmen] Everything that moves on the roads is heard on some mast. This is the season's, with where each part was heard.
[help,warm,their:linesmen] What you asked for is coming with a line-runner, {WRITER}. A voice is a road nobody has to walk, but some things still need carrying.
[help,cordial,their:linesmen] The relay can spare it, and a runner has it on the road.
[help,refusal,their:linesmen] The storms took three spans this season, {WRITER}, and every part we have is going up a mast. We have nothing to send.
[invitation,warm,their:linesmen] A lineman will come, and look at your heights while they are there.
[condolences,warm,their:linesmen] We put your dead's name down the whole line tonight, {WRITER}, mast to mast, so the region heard it. Every mast is a voice.
[condolences,cordial,their:linesmen] The Line is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. We have passed the news on true, and said where it was heard.
[warning,warm,their:linesmen] Your warning reached the relay before the trouble did, {WRITER}, and we called it down the line to everyone. The Line will not forget who said it first.
[warning,cordial,their:linesmen] We have your warning, {WRITER}, and it is on the line already. Keep it singing.
[greetings,warm,their:drillers] Your letter was read out in the union hall, {WRITER}, and somebody moved we write back at once, and it carried.
[greetings,cordial,their:drillers] The union has your letter, {WRITER}. It goes in the book with everything else.
[greetings,cool,their:drillers] We have your letter. The union will put it to the vote what we think of you.
[news,warm,their:drillers] Our carts go to every town that buys steel, {WRITER}, and our miners talk in every one of them. Here is the season's.
[news,cordial,their:drillers] There's always talk at the end of a shift. This is the part worth writing down.
[help,warm,their:drillers] What you asked for is coming with a pit-runner, {WRITER}. The vote was everyone for and nobody against.
[help,cordial,their:drillers] The union can spare it, and it is on the road.
[help,refusal,their:drillers] The seam ran thin this season, {WRITER}, and the union is feeding its own first. We have nothing to send, and the vote was not easy.
[invitation,warm,their:drillers] A driller will come, and look at your ground while they are there.
[condolences,warm,their:drillers] We stood a minute at the face for your dead this morning, {WRITER}, every shift. Everyone up at the end of the shift, we say, and we are sorry yours did not come up.
[condolences,cordial,their:drillers] The union is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. One book, one union, and your dead are in our book too.
[warning,warm,their:drillers] Your warning reached the pit in time, {WRITER}, and everyone was out of the shaft when it came. The union owes you, and it votes to pay.
[warning,cordial,their:drillers] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The headframe is manned tonight.
[greetings,warm,their:citizens] Your letter was read at the town hall, {WRITER}, and entered in the record with the minister's own note of thanks.
[greetings,cordial,their:citizens] The Republic has your letter, {WRITER}, and has filed it, as it files everything.
[greetings,cool,their:citizens] We have your letter. The Republic has not yet decided what you are to it.
[news,warm,their:citizens] The Republic's radio hears a great deal, {WRITER}, and broadcasts some of it. Here is the season's, as the archive has it.
[news,cordial,their:citizens] Every dispatch rider brings a report, and every report is filed. These are the season's.
[help,warm,their:citizens] What you asked for is coming with a dispatch rider, {WRITER}, with the proper form attached.
[help,cordial,their:citizens] The ration office can spare it, and it is on the road.
[help,refusal,their:citizens] The ration office is short this season, {WRITER}, and the Republic's own citizens come first by law. There is nothing to send.
[invitation,warm,their:citizens] A clerk will come, with papers you may find useful.
[condolences,warm,their:citizens] The Republic read your dead's name on the evening broadcast, {WRITER}, among its own. Everyone counted, everyone owed, and everyone remembered.
[condolences,cordial,their:citizens] The Republic is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. The name has been entered in the record.
[warning,warm,their:citizens] Your warning reached the town hall in time, {WRITER}, and the Civic Guard was on the walls when it came. The Republic never forgets a friend, and it never fell.
[warning,cordial,their:citizens] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The Guard is doubled tonight.
[greetings,warm,their:crew] Your letter was read on the bridge at the change of watch, {WRITER}, and logged with the captain's own word beside it.
[greetings,cordial,their:crew] The hull has your letter, {WRITER}. It is logged.
[greetings,cool,their:crew] We have your letter. It is logged, without comment, for now.
[news,warm,their:crew] The ship still listens to the sky, {WRITER}, and to the ground round the hull. Here is what the log holds for the season.
[news,cordial,their:crew] The watch writes down everything it sees. This is the season's log, the part that concerns you.
[help,warm,their:crew] What you asked for is coming with a deck-runner, {WRITER}. The ship provides, and we provide for the ship and its friends.
[help,cordial,their:crew] The quartermaster can spare it, and it is on its way.
[help,refusal,their:crew] Another system failed this season, {WRITER}, and everything the hull has is going into it. We have nothing to send, and the log records our regret.
[invitation,warm,their:crew] An ensign will come, in the ship's uniform, as the regulations say.
[condolences,warm,their:crew] We logged your dead at the change of watch tonight, {WRITER}, as we log our own, and the whole crew stood for them.
[condolences,cordial,their:crew] The Fleet is sorry for your loss, {WRITER}. It is logged, and it will be remembered as long as the log is kept.
[warning,warm,their:crew] Your warning reached the hull in time, {WRITER}, and every post was manned when it came. Holding position, and grateful.
[warning,cordial,their:crew] We have your warning, {WRITER}. The ship is at its stations tonight.
[arrive,their:linesmen] Word from the relay, and I'll tell you where it was heard.
[leave,their:linesmen] There's a span down past the ridge, so I'll be going.
[deliver,their:linesmen] From the relay, passed on true.
[arrive,their:drillers] Pit-runner, with word from the union hall.
[leave,their:drillers] The shift changes at dusk, and I'm on it.
[deliver,their:drillers] From the union, voted on and counted.
[arrive,their:citizens] Dispatch rider of the Republic, with a letter under seal.
[leave,their:citizens] I'm expected back at the town hall by evening, so I'll go.
[deliver,their:citizens] From the Republic, with the proper form.
[arrive,their:crew] Deck-runner from the hull, reporting with a message.
[leave,their:crew] My watch begins at the next bell, so I'll take my leave.
[deliver,their:crew] From the ship, logged and sealed.
[arrive,their:linesmen] Good height behind your walls, I'd put a mast on it.
[wait,their:linesmen] I've waited out worse at the top of a mast.
[stay,their:linesmen] A dry roof, and you can hear the wind in the wires from here.
[leave,their:linesmen] Keep it singing, and say where you heard it.
[pass,their:linesmen] Every mast is a voice, and every voice is a road nobody has to walk.
[arrive,their:drillers] Good rock under you, I can tell from the walls.
[wait,their:drillers] Miners wait for the cage every shift, take your time.
[stay,their:drillers] A hot supper and nobody needs a lamp, that's a good billet.
[leave,their:drillers] Everyone up at the end of the shift, and good day to you.
[pass,their:drillers] The ground keeps what it's given, remember that.
[arrive,their:citizens] Orderly streets, the Republic would approve.
[wait,their:citizens] The Republic is patient, and so am I.
[stay,their:citizens] A clean room and a quiet house, very civic.
[leave,their:citizens] The Republic never fell, and it thanks you for the bed.
[pass,their:citizens] Everyone counted, everyone owed.
[arrive,their:crew] Permission to come aboard, as we say.
[wait,their:crew] We have been waiting two hundred years, so an hour is nothing.
[stay,their:crew] A berth that doesn't hum, I could sleep a week.
[leave,their:crew] Holding position, and thank you for your hospitality.
[pass,their:crew] We were promised a world, and we are still waiting for orders to disembark.
[chat,them,their:linesmen] We fear silence more than storms, because silence is how the region fell apart.
[endwarm,them,their:linesmen] If you ever need a word carried, call it up a mast and ask for me.
[faithtalk,them,their:linesmen] Ennis Calloway walked the hills with a coil of copper, and his first mast is never quiet.
[chat,them,their:drillers] Nobody decides alone in the union, and nobody goes down alone either.
[endwarm,them,their:drillers] If your ground ever wants drilling, send for the union and ask for me.
[faithtalk,them,their:drillers] Marta Grieve put it to the vote when the seam ran dry, and we voted to stay together.
[chat,them,their:citizens] The Republic never fell, it simply has fewer citizens than it used to.
[endwarm,them,their:citizens] Come to the town hall one day, and I'll find you the right form myself.
[faithtalk,them,their:citizens] Clement Ashdown read the old laws on the radio each evening until other towns answered.
[chat,them,their:crew] We keep ship's time wherever we are, it is the only clock that never stopped.
[endwarm,them,their:crew] If the order ever comes, I'll see that your name is in the log.
[faithtalk,them,their:crew] Imre Sallow told us to keep our posts until the order came, and died before he gave it.

[opt0] A sleeper from the Fleet's caskets came to the gate at dusk, {X_nameDef}, two hundred years asleep and nobody left who knew them. We took them in. They held the gatepost a long time before they came through it.
[opt1] We gave the sleeper from the Fleet's hull a warm corner for the night. They asked me what year it was and didn't believe the answer.
[opt2] A sleeper from the Fleet's caskets asked us for shelter at dusk and we kept the gate shut. They said "holding position" as if it were an answer, and walked off.

gloomy.li: [opt0] Everyone they knew is two hundred years dead, and now they have us.
